Frequently Asked Questions

1. What should I understand first about bib cock?

Start with the intended application. Bib Cock should be selected by what the system needs to do, where it will be installed and the conditions it will operate under.

2. How do I choose the right bib cock?

Match dimensions, connection or mounting method, operating conditions and maintenance access to the site. Then compare models that meet those requirements.

3. Which specification matters most?

There is rarely one universal specification. Size, pressure class, outlet layout, mounting type or material may be the deciding factor depending on the product category.

4. Can I use a different product with a similar size?

Not automatically. Products with similar nominal dimensions can have different duties, connection methods or ratings. Confirm system compatibility first.

5. What is the most common buying mistake?

Choosing by appearance, price or nominal size before checking the actual site, related components and installation requirements.

6. Should an installer be involved before purchase?

Yes for concealed plumbing, drainage, borewell, structural mounting and other work where an incorrect choice would require expensive rework.

7. How important is maintenance access?

Very important. Valves, traps, cartridges, joints and serviceable parts should remain reachable where future maintenance is expected.

8. How can I compare two models fairly?

Use the same criteria for both: application, dimensions, material, connection, operating rating, warranty/support and service access.

9. Does a higher price always mean better suitability?

No. A premium product can still be wrong for a particular installation. Suitability comes from matching the specification to the requirement.
